::: {.callout-important}
## Synthetic data

This project contains synthetic data and analysis created for demonstration
purposes only. Aurora Lending Group is a fictional company; no real borrower,
portfolio or performance data was used.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## AI-generated content

The commentary and business scenarios in this report were generated by AI for
illustration and have not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.
:::

```{python}
# | label: setup
import json
import os
import re

import awswrangler as wr
import boto3
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from great_tables import GT, loc, style

# This report is deployed to Posit Connect as a self-contained document, so it
# does not import the repo's config.py -- that file is not in the bundle. The
# settings it needs are declared here, and every one accepts an environment
# variable override so Connect can point the report at another account.
# tests/test_report_config.py makes sure these still agree with config.py.
REGION = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_REGION", "us-east-2")
WORKGROUP = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_WORKGROUP", "primary")
DATABASE = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_DATABASE", "aurora_lending")
ENDPOINT = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_ENDPOINT", "aurora-lending-risk")
BUCKET_PREFIX = "sagemaker-posit-conf-2026-demo"

session = boto3.Session(region_name=REGION)

# The account number is read from STS rather than written down, so this public
# repository holds no account identifier and a fork needs no edit.
BUCKET = os.environ.get("POSIT_DEMO_BUCKET") or (
    f"{BUCKET_PREFIX}-"
    f"{session.client('sts').get_caller_identity()['Account']}-{REGION}"
)
ATHENA_STAGING = f"s3://{BUCKET}/athena-query-results/"

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.dpi": 140, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.25, "font.size": 9,
})
POSIT_BLUE, POSIT_ORANGE, POSIT_BURGUNDY = "#447099", "#ee6331", "#9a4665"


def athena(sql: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return wr.athena.read_sql_query(
        sql,
        database=DATABASE,
        workgroup=WORKGROUP,
        s3_output=ATHENA_STAGING,
        boto3_session=session,
        # ctas_approach=False: the default creates temporary Glue tables, which
        # needs Glue write permission the read-only demo role does not have.
        ctas_approach=False,
    )
```

```{python}
# | label: load
loans = athena("""
    SELECT f.loan_id,
           f.origination_date,
           f.fico_at_origination,
           f.dti,
           f.apr,
           f.term_months,
           CAST(f.principal_amount AS double)    AS principal_amount,
           CAST(f.outstanding_balance AS double) AS outstanding_balance,
           f.employment_length_years,
           f.purpose,
           f.charged_off,
           b.state,
           b.income_band
    FROM fct_loan_performance f
    JOIN dim_borrower b ON b.borrower_id = f.borrower_id
""")

loans["vintage"] = pd.to_datetime(loans["origination_date"]).dt.year
loans["fico_band"] = pd.cut(
    loans["fico_at_origination"],
    bins=[579, 620, 660, 700, 740, 780, 850],
    labels=["580-619", "620-659", "660-699", "700-739", "740-779", "780+"],
)

originated = loans["principal_amount"].sum()
outstanding = loans["outstanding_balance"].sum()
chargeoff_rate = loans["charged_off"].mean()
```

## Portfolio at a glance

The book holds **`{python} f"{len(loans):,}"`** loans originated between
`{python} int(loans["vintage"].min())` and `{python} int(loans["vintage"].max())`,
totalling **`{python} f"${originated/1e6:,.0f}M"`** advanced and
**`{python} f"${outstanding/1e6:,.0f}M"`** still outstanding. The realised
charge-off rate is **`{python} f"{chargeoff_rate*100:.1f}%"`**.

Data is queried live from Amazon Athena at render time; nothing is extracted or
cached.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-purpose
by_purpose = (
    loans.groupby("purpose")
    .agg(loans=("loan_id", "size"),
         originated=("principal_amount", "sum"),
         avg_apr=("apr", "mean"),
         avg_fico=("fico_at_origination", "mean"),
         chargeoff=("charged_off", "mean"))
    .sort_values("chargeoff", ascending=False)
    .reset_index()
)
by_purpose["purpose"] = by_purpose["purpose"].str.replace("_", " ").str.title()

(
    GT(by_purpose)
    .tab_header(title="Performance by loan purpose",
                subtitle="Ordered by realised charge-off rate")
    .cols_label(purpose="Purpose", loans="Loans", originated="Originated",
                avg_apr="Avg APR", avg_fico="Avg FICO", chargeoff="Charge-off rate")
    .fmt_number(columns="loans", decimals=0, use_seps=True)
    .fmt_currency(columns="originated", currency="USD", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns=["avg_apr", "chargeoff"], decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns="avg_fico", decimals=0)
    .data_color(columns="chargeoff", palette=["#ffffff", POSIT_ORANGE])
    .tab_style(style=style.text(weight="bold"), locations=loc.column_labels())
    .tab_source_note("Synthetic data, generated for demonstration purposes.")
)
```

Small business lending carries the highest realised loss rate, and auto
refinance the lowest -- the spread is wide enough that purpose alone is a
meaningful segmentation for pricing review.

## Where the risk sits

```{python}
# | label: fig-risk
# | fig-cap: "Charge-off concentration by credit quality and origination vintage."
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))

band = loans.groupby("fico_band", observed=True)["charged_off"].mean() * 100
band.plot.bar(ax=ax1, color=POSIT_BLUE, rot=0, width=0.72)
ax1.set(title="By FICO band at origination", xlabel="", ylabel="charge-off rate (%)")

vintage = loans.pivot_table(index="vintage", columns="fico_band",
                            values="charged_off", observed=True) * 100
vintage.plot(ax=ax2, marker="o", linewidth=1.5, colormap="viridis")
ax2.set(title="By origination vintage", xlabel="", ylabel="")
ax2.legend(title="FICO band", fontsize=6.5, ncol=2, frameon=False)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Credit quality dominates: the weakest band loses roughly
`{python} f"{band.iloc[0]/band.iloc[-1]:.0f}"`x what the strongest does. Recent
vintages are less seasoned, so their realised rates understate lifetime loss.

## Model-scored risk

```{python}
# | label: score
# | output: false
FEATURES = ["fico_at_origination", "dti", "apr", "term_months",
            "principal_amount", "employment_length_years", "purpose"]

sample = loans.sample(min(2_000, len(loans)), random_state=20260821).copy()
endpoint_available = True
endpoint_error = ""

# The endpoint only exists around demo time. If it has been torn down, this
# report still needs to render on Connect -- so the failure is captured and
# reported in-line rather than aborting the build.
try:
    body = json.dumps({"instances": sample[FEATURES].to_dict(orient="records")})
    response = session.client("sagemaker-runtime").invoke_endpoint(
        EndpointName=ENDPOINT, ContentType="application/json", Body=body
    )
    sample["risk_score"] = json.loads(response["Body"].read())["predictions"]
except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - any failure degrades the same way
    endpoint_available = False
    # AWS error text repeats the account number. This report gets published,
    # so the number is masked before it reaches the page.
    endpoint_error = re.sub(
        r"\b\d{12}\b", "<account>", f"{type(err).__name__}: {err}"
    )
```

```{python}
# | label: score-note
# | output: asis
if not endpoint_available:
    print(":::: {.callout-warning}\n")
    print("## Model scores unavailable\n")
    print(
        f"The SageMaker endpoint `{ENDPOINT}` did not respond, so this "
        "section is omitted. Everything above is queried directly from Athena "
        "and is unaffected.\n"
    )
    print(
        f"Deploy it with `uv run python ml/train_and_deploy.py --domain "
        f"{"finance"}`, then re-render.\n"
    )
    print(f"> `{endpoint_error}`\n")
    print("::::\n")
```

```{python}
# | label: tbl-lift
if endpoint_available:
    sample["decile"] = pd.qcut(sample["risk_score"], 10, labels=False,
                               duplicates="drop") + 1
    lift = (
        sample.groupby("decile")
        .agg(loans=("loan_id", "size"),
             predicted=("risk_score", "mean"),
             actual=("charged_off", "mean"),
             exposure=("outstanding_balance", "sum"))
        .sort_index(ascending=False)
        .reset_index()
    )
    out = (
        GT(lift)
        .tab_header(title="Predicted versus realised charge-off by risk decile",
                    subtitle=f"{len(sample):,} loans scored on endpoint "
                             f"{ENDPOINT}")
        .cols_label(decile="Decile", loans="Loans", predicted="Predicted",
                    actual="Realised", exposure="Outstanding")
        .fmt_number(columns="loans", decimals=0, use_seps=True)
        .fmt_percent(columns=["predicted", "actual"], decimals=1)
        .fmt_currency(columns="exposure", currency="USD", decimals=0)
        .data_color(columns="actual", palette=["#ffffff", POSIT_BURGUNDY])
        .tab_style(style=style.text(weight="bold"), locations=loc.column_labels())
        .tab_source_note("Decile 10 is the highest predicted risk. "
                         "Synthetic data, generated for demonstration purposes.")
    )
else:
    out = None
out
```

```{python}
# | label: summary
# | output: asis
if endpoint_available:
    base = sample["charged_off"].mean() * 100
    top = lift.loc[lift["decile"] == 10, "actual"].iloc[0] * 100
    captured = (sample.loc[sample["decile"] >= 9, "charged_off"].sum()
                / max(sample["charged_off"].sum(), 1) * 100)
    at_risk = sample.loc[sample["decile"] >= 9, "outstanding_balance"].sum()
    print(
        f"The model separates the book cleanly. Against a portfolio base rate of "
        f"**{base:.1f}%**, the riskiest decile realises **{top:.1f}%** -- "
        f"**{top/base:.1f}x** base. The top two deciles capture "
        f"**{captured:.0f}%** of all charge-offs while holding "
        f"**${at_risk/1e6:,.1f}M** of outstanding balance, which is where "
        f"collections and line-management attention earns the most.\n\n"
        f"Predicted and realised rates track closely across every decile, so the "
        f"scores can be used as levels rather than only as a ranking."
    )
```

## Method

Data is generated synthetically, published to Amazon S3 as parquet, and
registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. This report queries it through Amazon
Athena at render time and scores a sample against a logistic risk model hosted
on a SageMaker real-time endpoint. The whole workflow -- query, model, report --
runs from Positron on Amazon SageMaker and publishes to Posit Connect.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Reproducing this report

```bash
uv run python data/generate.py     --domain finance
uv run python load/load_athena.py  --domain finance
uv run python ml/train_and_deploy.py --domain finance
quarto render reports/aurora_lending/portfolio_risk_review.qmd
uv run python ml/teardown.py --all
```
:::
